decision.explanation: A block upper triangular matrix must admit a nontrivial partition into square diagonal blocks with zeros in every block below them. For either possible partition of A, the lower-left block contains 4; for either partition of B, it contains 5. The only nontrivial partition of C has lower-left entry 1. Thus none is block upper triangular.

after.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a block diagonal matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & y & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & z & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & y & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & z & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 10 \\ 2 & y & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & z\end{aligned}|\cdot 3 \\  & =8\cdot 3 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The matrix is block diagonal, so its determinant is the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants: (3/5)(-25) = -15.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
Notice that we have a block diagonal matrix. Therefore, its determinant is equal to the product of the diagonal blocks' determinants:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}r & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 3t & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -25\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}r & 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 3t & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -25\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}r & 1 \\ 5 & 3t\end{aligned}|\cdot (-25) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\cdot (-25) \\  & =-15.\end{aligned}
$$
